title: School access can be interrupted at population scale without a single explanation
source_unit: U.S. Department of Education Ed Data Express chronic-absenteeism administrative file for school year 2022-23
geography: United States and state education agencies; school year 2022-23

denominator.unit: students in the national state-level chronic-absenteeism file

chronically_absent.unit: students absent at least 10% of enrolled school days

observations.method: Department of Education state-level administrative reporting under the ESEA/ESSA chronic-absenteeism data collection; chronic absence is defined as absence for 10% or more of school days.
observations.uncertainty: The file is an aggregate administrative measure and does not identify each student's reason, support, learning, safety, belonging, or later attendance outcome.
observations.subgroup: Students reported by state education agencies; the file includes state and subgroup data with privacy protections.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high chronic-absence count does not prove permanent departure, academic failure, school failure, or one common cause.

reported_range_examples.value: 22.6% Alabama; 27.7% California; 41.2% Arizona; 43.1% New Mexico; 46.7% District of Columbia

observations.method: Descriptive comparison of state-level percentages in the Department of Education chronic-absence file.
observations.uncertainty: Differences can reflect reporting, enrollment, calendar, policy, student composition, and lived conditions; the comparison does not identify causes or rank school quality.
observations.subgroup: State education agencies reporting all-student chronic-absence percentages.
observations.counterinterpretation: A state percentage is not a causal estimate and cannot show that a particular transportation, housing, safety, or engagement intervention would change attendance.

related_sources.claim: The Department of Education defines chronic absence and publishes the underlying state, local, and school files with data notes.

boundary: This record measures aggregate chronic absence and descriptive state variation for SY 2022-23. It does not establish causes, school response, learning, safety, belonging, or durable student return.
